correctness.rationale: For every even m and any normalized rank-one real-Hilbert operator, T^m=c^(m-1)T. The positive-trace 2x2 block has determinant 1+a^m and Frobenius squared 2+2a^m+a^(2m-2); exact singular-value arithmetic gives the displayed F_m. Degree-two differentiation identifies the unique optimum and the rationalized quadratic stability. For the even-degree limit, a uniform exponential tail excludes escape of the scaled overlap, compact-uniform convergence identifies the limiting f(c)=c/(2e^c+1), and its unique critical point is 1+W(1/(2e)). The proof covers all normalized rank-one operators and endpoints; no numerical extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The 2026 qualitative square-property equivalence motivates an exact failure benchmark on canonical uniformly convex spaces; an all-even-degree extremal envelope is a natural quantitative strengthening of that test. The exact square value and quadratic stability measure optimal non-Daugavet overlap, and the Lambert boundary layer shows sharp inverse-degree deterioration of the largest positive-gap witness. These quantify natural geometry rather than arbitrary isolated small examples, with complete parameter coverage across even degrees.
